title: `lateinit` defers a non-nullable object property's first assignment past the constructor
scope:
one new property modifier, `lateinit`, usable only on a non-nullable, class/interface-typed
property. Nothing else changes: scalar-typed properties, `?T` properties, locals, and every other rule
`rule:classes/definite-property-initialization` states keep working exactly as before.

summary.headline: `lateinit` lets a container assign a property after construction
summary.body:
A property marked `lateinit` is excused from the constructor-must-assign rule, for containers
and ORMs that fill an object after `new` returns. The property stays as non-nullable as any
other, and reading it before its first write throws a catchable error. It is allowed only on a
non-nullable class or interface type — a scalar has a free default like `= 0`, and `?T` already
means "may be empty" — and never with `readonly`, whose write-once promise is the opposite. The
price is a second way a read can fail at run time.
